Subject: POC trial planning: workload intake & success criteria (AcmeHealth)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC scheduled: 

Summary / Success criteria (what AcmeHealth wants to validate):
- Accuracy: average intent classification precision >= 92% on your validation set.
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency < 350ms for typical prompts (~150 tokens).
- Cost: target unit cost <= $0.003 per generated token at your expected concurrency and batching.
- Stability: model handles daily traffic profile with spikes (details below) without error-rate spikes > 0.5%.

POC scope and timeline:
- Duration: 2 weeks of live testing + 1 week evaluation (total 3 weeks).
- Proposed kickoff: week of Jun 14 (dependent on data ingest).
- Owners: Marissa (sales lead) + Ben (SE) on Redwood side; Alex + Priya on Acme side.

Workload intake we need from you to size the trial and config autoscaling:
- Average RPS (requests per second) and peak RPS during business hours
- Expected concurrency (how many simultaneous sessions/users)
- Typical prompt length (input tokens) and average generated tokens per response
- Burst patterns: frequency and duration of spikes (minutes/hours, expected multiplier)
- Percent of long-running prompts ( > 1000 tokens )

If you can send the workload profile CSV (or just paste numbers) and the dataset we should use for the accuracy checks, we can firm up instance sizing and an estimated cost for the trial. I attached a short success_criteria template to fill in (poc_success_criteria.xlsx).

Next steps:
1) Alex — share workload_profile.csv and validation dataset by EOD Thu Jun 3
2) Ben — will propose an infra config and preliminary cost estimate once we have the numbers
3) Marissa — lock trial kickoff date once infra and onboarding times are confirmed

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Alex / Marissa —

Thanks for the profile, Alex — that's very helpful. A few technical clarifications so we can size correctly and give a conservative cost estimate:

1) RPS vs requests that require stateful context (session-based KV cache):
- What percent of requests will include prior conversation context (session_id present and stateful)? (This affects KV cache hit rates and memory footprint.)

2) Distribution of token lengths:
- Can you confirm approximate percentiles? (p10/p50/p90/p99) based on the CSV — if not available, ballpark is fine.

3) Burst behavior:
- For the 5x monthly sweep (20 minutes) — is traffic coming from many users in parallel or a single batch process? If single batch, we may route that to a different processing queue.

4) SLAs and error handling:
- What's your tolerance for fallback to a cheaper model variant during sustained capacity constraints?

Example sizing assumptions I'll test:
- Baseline: 20 rps sustained; peak 120 rps; concurrency 200 -> likely need a small dedicated pool with autoscaling to cover peaks unless you want to rely on hosted fallback.
- Token profile: median prompt 65 / median generation 85 -> estimate tokens per request ~150.

If you can share the CSV (thanks for attaching) and the validation dataset, I'll run a quick sim and follow up with two recommended configs (hosted + dedicated sample) and an estimated per-token trial cost.

I'll aim to send the config options by Fri Jun 4 EOD.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwoodinference.com
